26-sf2-bm-2347.trick: 25% is just ¼, so take a quarter of 1,600 twice: 400, then 100.

26-sf2-bm-2756.solution: For F = ai + bj, the magnitude is √(a² + b²). Here √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 N.
26-sf2-bm-2756.trick: 8, 15, 17 is a well known right-angled triple (64 + 225 = 289), so the magnitude is 17 without squaring anything.

26-sf2-bm-2759.solution: For each gene, Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, Aa, aa, so ¾ of offspring show the dominant trait. The two genes assort independently, so the chance of both is ¾ × ¾ = 9/16.
26-sf2-bm-2759.trick: Recall the 9:3:3:1 ratio out of 16. The 9 is both dominant, so 9/16. The 1/16 option is both recessive, and 3/16 is only one of the mixed classes.

26-sf2-bm-2762.solution: 30 years ÷ 10 years = 3 half-lives. Each half-life halves what is left, so the fraction remaining is (½)³ = 1/8.
26-sf2-bm-2762.trick: 30 ÷ 10 = 3 halvings: ½, then ¼, then ⅛. The ¼ option would be 20 years and 1/16 would be 40 years.

26-sf2-bm-2766.solution: A 25% discount means paying 75%, so one TV costs 0.75 × $8,000 = $6,000. For 24 TVs the total is 24 × $6,000 = $144,000.
26-sf2-bm-2766.trick: Paying ¾ of the price for 24 TVs is the same as paying full price for 18 TVs, because ¾ of 24 is 18. Then 18 × 8 = 144, so $144,000.

26-sf2-bm-2770.trick: 4² is 16, and 100 − 16 = 84. Only one option has 84 under the root, so you can stop there.

26-sf2-bm-2775.solution: Relative error = absolute error ÷ measured value = 0.2 ÷ 50 = 0.004. As a percentage that is 0.004 × 100 = 0.4%.
26-sf2-bm-2775.trick: Double both numbers: 0.2 ÷ 50 = 0.4 ÷ 100, which is 0.4%. An error of 0.2 on 50 is tiny, so the 24% and 25% options cannot be right.

26-sf2-bm-2778.solution: This is the logistic equation dP/dt = rP(1 − P/K), where K is the carrying capacity. Comparing with 25P(1 − P/100) gives r = 25 and K = 100. Growth stops when 1 − P/100 = 0, which gives P = 100. So the carrying capacity is 100.
26-sf2-bm-2778.trick: In dP/dt = rP(1 − P/K), K is the number under P inside the bracket, so it is 100. The 25 is the growth rate, and 50 is only half of K.

26-sf2-bm-2784.solution: For z = a + bi the modulus is |z| = √(a² + b²). So |−3 + 4i| = √((−3)² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.
26-sf2-bm-2784.trick: Spot the 3, 4, 5 right-angled triangle. The minus sign does not matter, so the modulus is 5.

26-sf2-bm-2787.solution: R(x) = −2x² + 20x + 50 is a downward parabola, so its maximum is at the vertex x = −b ÷ 2a = −20 ÷ (−4) = 5. Then R(5) = −2(25) + 20(5) + 50 = −50 + 100 + 50 = 100.

26-sf2-bm-2797.solution: For each gene, Aa × Aa gives ¾ dominant offspring. The three genes assort independently, so P(all three dominant) = (¾)³ = 27/64.
26-sf2-bm-2797.trick: Cube the ¾ from each gene: 3³ = 27 and 4³ = 64, so 27/64. The 1/64 option is the all recessive case.

26-sf2-bm-2802.solution: Pipe A fills 1/6 of the tank each hour and pipe B empties 1/8 each hour. Net rate = 1/6 − 1/8 = 4/24 − 3/24 = 1/24 of the tank per hour. So the tank fills in 24 hours.
26-sf2-bm-2802.trick: Use product over difference: 6 × 8 ÷ (8 − 6) = 48 ÷ 2 = 24. This works whenever one pipe fills, one empties, and the filling pipe is the faster one.

26-sf2-bm-2806.solution: Expected number = number of bulbs × defective rate = 4,000 × 0.005 = 20 bulbs.
26-sf2-bm-2806.trick: 0.005 is half of 1%. 1% of 4,000 is 40, so half of that is 20.

26-sf2-bm-2810.solution: The water added is the integral of the rate from t = 1 to t = 3. ∫(6t + 4) dt = 3t² + 4t, so the amount is (3 × 3² + 4 × 3) − (3 × 1² + 4 × 1) = (27 + 12) − (3 + 4) = 39 − 7 = 32 litres.
26-sf2-bm-2810.trick: The rate climbs steadily from R(1) = 10 to R(3) = 22 L/min, so over 2 minutes the total is between 20 and 44. That rules out 16 and 48. For the exact value, the average rate is (10 + 22) ÷ 2 = 16, and 16 × 2 = 32.

26-sf2-bm-2817.solution: The minus sign vanishes when squared. So the magnitude is √(7² + (−24)²) = √(49 + 576) = √625 = 25.
26-sf2-bm-2817.trick: 7, 24, 25 is a well known right-angled triple (49 + 576 = 625), so the answer is 25 without squaring anything.

26-sf2-bm-2822.solution: Let the number be x. Then (x − 18) × 6 = 60, so x − 18 = 60 ÷ 6 = 10. Therefore x = 10 + 18 = 28.

26-sf2-bm-2828.solution: A scale of 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm on the ground. So 8 cm is 8 × 50,000 = 400,000 cm. Since 100,000 cm = 1 km, that is 400,000 ÷ 100,000 = 4 km.
26-sf2-bm-2828.trick: Each map centimetre is 50,000 cm, which is 500 m, or half a kilometre. So 8 cm is half of 8, which is 4 km.

26-sf2-bm-2831.solution: The projectile is on the ground when h(t) = 0. So −5t² + 30t = −5t(t − 6) = 0, which gives t = 0 (the launch) or t = 6. It lands after 6 seconds.
26-sf2-bm-2831.trick: Cancel one t from −5t² + 30t = 0 to get 5t = 30, so t = 6. In general, for h = −at² + bt the landing time is b ÷ a.

26-sf2-bm-2839.solution: The extra pay is 25% of his current pay: 0.25 × $600 = $150 per month.

26-sf2-bm-2843.solution: The question does not say where the 30° is measured. Taking it as the angle between the tree and the ground, the height is the side opposite it, so height = 500 × sin 30° = 500 × 0.5 = 250 m. If it were measured from the wall, the height would be 500 × cos 30° ≈ 433 m, which is not an option. So the answer is 250 m.
26-sf2-bm-2843.trick: sin 30° is exactly ½, so the height is half of 500, which is 250 m. The 1,000 m option is longer than the tree itself, so it is impossible.
26-sf2-bm-2843.computed: 250 m (if 30° is the angle with the ground; about 433 m if it is the angle with the wall)
26-sf2-bm-2843.comment: The question does not say whether the 30° is measured from the ground or from the wall. From the ground the height is 500 sin 30° = 250 m (the show's answer, and the only workable option), but from the wall it would be 500 cos 30° ≈ 433 m, which is not offered.
